key_insight: Model optimization should be chosen as a constraint-driven, multi-objective engineering decision across latency, memory, accuracy, data, and retraining limits—not as a one-size-fits-all algorithm choice.
engineering_relevance: The framework helps teams match compression and acceleration techniques to real deployment conditions in cloud, edge, and enterprise systems.
method: Define five interacting constraint dimensions: data availability, latency budget, memory budget, accuracy tolerance, retraining budget.
Map optimization techniques such as quantization, pruning, distillation, PEFT, and inference-time optimization to the constraints they best relieve.
Provide decision pipelines for four representative industrial scenarios to guide practical selection.
evidence_signal: The paper synthesizes empirical gains reported across recent literature and selects methods based on measurable improvements against deployment bottlenecks.
watch_item: The framework is synthesis-driven, so real-world results may vary depending on model architecture, hardware, and workload-specific tradeoffs.
paper_title: Constraint-Driven Model Optimization: An Industry Framework for Selecting Compression and Acceleration Techniques in Modern Machine Learning Systems
